basis: Combined immunodeficiency with deficient immunoglobulin production; infections do not establish common direct damage to another organ.
Neoplasm occupying the trigeminal nerve; facial sensory loss and masticatory weakness reflect nerve dysfunction.
Benign neoplasm of the hard palate, an oral cavity site.
Cardiac Gaucher variant; thrombocytopenia and corneal opacity each 30-79%; hepatic involvement (30-79%) omitted at cap. Most neurologic findings are below 30%.
Disease of the third cranial nerve; impaired eye movements arise from neurologic dysfunction.
Larval Taenia tissue infection; CNS, ocular and subcutaneous sites vary by species, without a securely established 30% frequency across the umbrella.
Inherited macrothrombocytopenia and platelet dysfunction; mucosal bleeding and bruising do not establish separate organ damage.
Anterior horn motor neuron disease; denervation causes defining scapular and peroneal skeletal muscle atrophy in most patients.
Infantile interstitial lung disease; local glycogen-containing cells do not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
Lipoprotein metabolism disorder; hepatic steatosis and intestinal or neurologic damage vary substantially by subtype and are not established across most of the umbrella.
Maternal alloantibodies destroy fetal platelets; intracranial, urinary and gastrointestinal hemorrhage each occur in fewer than 30%.
Defining craniofacial and epiphyseal dysplasia with neurologic manifestations; hydrocephalus and spinal cord compression occur in 80-99%.
Defined principally by psychomotor and language delay and seizures; ocular abnormalities are reported without evidence of a 30% frequency.
Substance-use psychiatric concept; organ injuries from particular substances require separate disease diagnoses.
Neurologic movement disorder defined by motor and vocal tics; neurotransmitter dysfunction does not establish a metabolic disease.
Riboflavin transporter deficiency with neuropathy and defining sensorineural deafness; denervation muscle atrophy occurs in most. Optic atrophy is annotated below 30%.
Syndrome defined by Friedreich-type neurologic ataxia and congenital glaucoma; additional systemic involvement is not established for this concept.
PEX11B peroxisomal disorder; developmental impairment/neuropathy, congenital cataracts and hearing impairment recur in most described patients; evidence comes from small series.
Familial hyperpigmentation affects nasal skin, rather than the nasal airway.
Inherited platelet collagen-receptor dysfunction causing impaired aggregation and bleeding; bruising and epistaxis do not establish other organ damage.
ZIC2-related forebrain malformation; clefting is below 30%, and the supplied evidence does not establish endocrine dysfunction at 30% for this subtype.
Usually infectious inflammation of the epididymis, a reproductive organ outside the anatomical axes; associated urinary infection is a separate disease.
Inherited qualitative von Willebrand factor dysfunction causing a coagulation disorder; mucocutaneous bleeding does not establish other organ damage.
Localized cutaneous mucinosis producing nodules; the name does not imply thyroid disease or systemic endocrine dysfunction.
Prolonged myocardial contractile dysfunction following transient severe ischemia.
